key_insight: A synaptic weight depends on both the device’s stored internal state and the protocol used to read it, so identical measured outputs can conceal different states.
engineering_relevance: Reliable characterization of memristors, perovskite memlumors, and electrochemical transistors requires separating state storage from readout sensitivity.
method: Separate history-dependent internal states from observation maps using Chua’s memristive-systems framework.
Compare electrical, optical, and gate-controlled writing and reading across three device platforms.
Define synaptic weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes OECT states that produce equal channel currents at one drain bias but separate at another, and cites experiments revealing trapped charges in perovskite memlumors through read-write-read measurements.
watch_item: A single readout condition can mask stored-state differences; the abstract reports no AI model evaluation or solar-cell efficiency results.
paper_title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
